# The world as the Samhan named it: place, region and people names, 6th–7th centuries

Research report for the chronicle's world map (cosmology layer). Compiled Nov 2026.

## How to read this

**The big caveat.** The Samguk Sagi (三國史記) was compiled in 1145 and the Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) around 1280. Both drew on older records, but they can relabel places in later terms. Where a name also appears in something written during the Three Kingdoms era (a stele, a wooden tablet, a Chinese history of the time, Hyecho's diary), that is noted. A name that shows up only in the Goryeo compilations is flagged.

**Confidence key** (used in every table):

- **A**: in a source written in the 5th–8th centuries (epigraphy, mokgan, Sui/Tang-era histories, Hyecho, Yijing, the Nihon Shoki of 720).
- **B**: only in the Samguk Sagi or Samguk Yusa, but probably from an older record (dated annal entry, quoted document).
- **C**: in the Goryeo compilations but anachronistic or later for 6th–7th-century use.
- **M**: myth or oral tradition. The age of the motif is uncertain, and it is usually recorded late.

A dagger (†) marks a detail taken from standard references that was **not re-checked** in this session. Everything else was checked against the online text or a database entry linked under Sources.

**Source dates at a glance**

| Source | Date | What it gives the map |
|---|---|---|
| Gwanggaeto Stele 廣開土王碑 | 414 | Goguryeo's own world: Buyeo, Baekje, Silla, Wa, Gaya, Khitan tribes, "Four Seas" |
| Moduru epitaph 牟頭婁墓誌 | 5th c. | "All under heaven, the four quarters" 天下四方 |
| Jungwon (Chungju) Goguryeo Stele 中原高句麗碑 | 5th c. | Silla's king as "the Eastern Yi maegeum" 東夷寐錦 |
| Silla Jinheung stelae 眞興王碑 | 550s–568 | Silla's frontier: Changnyeong, Bukhansan, Hwangchoryeong, Maunryeong |
| Liang tribute scroll 梁職貢圖 | c. 526–539 | Baekje's "side states"; Persian and Baekje envoys in one scroll |
| Book of Sui 隋書 | 636 | Mohe tribes, Tamna, mixed population of Baekje, Wa letter |
| Old and New Books of Tang 舊/新唐書 | 945 / 1060, from Tang archives | "Three kingdoms east of the sea", Land of Giants |
| Yijing 義淨, 大唐西域求法高僧傳 | 691 | Korean monks in India, Srivijaya, on the Tibet road; Indian name for Goguryeo |
| Hyecho 慧超, 往五天竺國傳 | 727 (Dunhuang ms. P.3532) | The Korean eyewitness west: India, Persia, Arabs, Fulin, Turks, Tibet, Sogdiana |
| Afrasiab mural, Samarkand | c. 660s | Goguryeo envoys in feathered caps at a Sogdian court |
| Kül Tegin inscription | 732 | Turkic name for Goguryeo: Bökli |
| Nihon Shoki 日本書紀 | 720 | Japanese names for Korean places and for the Sui/Tang court |
| Samguk Sagi 三國史記 | 1145 | The annals; most dated attestations |
| Samguk Yusa 三國遺事 | c. 1280 | Myths, Buddhist geography, the Hwangnyongsa "nine enemies" |

## 1. Peninsula and near neighbours

| Name | Hanja / Korean | Gloss | Modern identification | Earliest attestation | Conf. / caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Malgal (Mohe) | 靺鞨 말갈 | the forest-and-river peoples of the northeast | Tungusic groups, Songhua–Ussuri–Amur basins | Book of Sui 81 lists seven tribes: 粟末 Sokmal, 伯咄, 安車骨, 拂涅, 號室, 黑水 Heuksu, 白山 Baeksan †. Samguk Yusa (Jajang): Silla "touches the Malgal to the north" 北連靺鞨 | A. The Samguk Sagi has Malgal raiding Baekje and Silla in the 1st–3rd centuries. That is anachronistic: the name appears in Chinese sources only from the 6th c. Most scholars read those early "Malgal" as Ye 濊 or East Ye. Fine for 6th–7th c. scenes. |
| Mulgil | 勿吉 물길 | earlier name of the Mohe | same region, 5th c. | Book of Wei †; Samguk Sagi, Munjamyeong 3 (494): Buyeo's king surrenders to Goguryeo after Mulgil pressure † | A/B. A 5th-century name; don't use it for the 7th. |
| Suksin | 肅愼 숙신 (息愼) | the ancient northeastern people | classical label for the far northeast | Gwanggaeto Stele (息愼 †); Samguk Sagi, Seocheon 11 (280) † | A as a classical label. Archaic by the 7th c. |
| Khitan | 契丹 거란 | steppe people west of Goguryeo | Shira Muren basin, Inner Mongolia | Gwanggaeto Stele, year 395 campaign against 稗麗 (Baeryeo, read as a Khitan tribe) †; Samguk Sagi, Sosurim 8 (378), Khitan raid the north †; Tang edict to Uija, 651: "order the Khitan and other tribes to cross the Liao marshes" 即令契丹諸蕃渡遼澤 | A. Solid. Used by the Tang as auxiliaries against Goguryeo. |
| Shiwei | 室韋 실위 | forest-steppe people north of the Khitan | Greater Khingan / Nen River | Book of Wei, Book of Sui; the Sui says southern Shiwei got their iron from Goguryeo † | A for Chinese sources. Not found in the Samguk Sagi. One of the routes proposed for the Afrasiab envoys runs through Shiwei land. |
| Xi / Gomakhae | 奚 / 庫莫奚 해 | Khitan cousins | west of the Khitan | Chinese histories; listed among peoples the Turks pressed in the 550s (KHDB note to Yangwon 7) | A (Chinese only). Minor. |
| Rouran | 柔然, 蠕蠕 유연/연연 | the steppe empire before the Turks | Mongolia, to 552–555 | Baekje's letter to Northern Wei (472), in the Samguk Sagi (Gaero 18): Goguryeo "allies north with the 蠕蠕" † | A (the letter is in the Book of Wei). For any scene before 552. |
| Buyeo | 夫餘 부여 (北夫餘, 東夫餘) | the parent kingdom | Songhua basin, Jilin | Gwanggaeto Stele: Chumo "came out of Northern Buyeo" 出自北夫餘; 410 campaign against 東夫餘. Moduru epitaph: 元出北夫餘 | A. Gone by 494 as a state; alive as a lineage claim. Baekje's royal surname is 夫餘/扶餘 and Baekje renamed itself 南扶餘 in 538. |
| Okjeo | 沃沮 옥저 (東沃沮, 北沃沮) | "wet fields" | Hamgyeong coast | Sanguozhi (3rd c.); Samguk Sagi, Taejo 4 (56) † | A for the 3rd c. Long absorbed into Goguryeo; archaic by the 7th. |
| Ye / East Ye | 濊, 東濊 예/동예 | the eastern coast people | Gangwon coast | Sanguozhi; Samguk Sagi, Jinheung 9 (548): "Goguryeo and the 穢人 attack Baekje's Doksan fortress" | A/B. Ye-maek 濊貊 survives as a broad ethnonym. |
| Usan-guk | 于山國 우산국 | island country | Ulleungdo (+ islets) | Samguk Sagi, Silla Jijeung 13 (512), 6th month: "于山國歸服 … 在溟州正東海島 或名鬱陵島". Isabu's wooden lions | B. Well-known passage; the one-line source is the Samguk Sagi. |
| Tamna | 耽羅 탐라; also 耽牟羅, 聃牟羅, 乇羅/托羅, 涉羅, 儋羅 | "island country" | Jeju | Samguk Sagi, Baekje Munju 2 (476): 耽羅國獻方物. Book of Sui / Bei shi, Baekje: "three months' sail south is 耽牟羅國, rich in deer, a dependency of Baekje". Silla Munmu 2 (662): Tamna's lord 徒冬音律 submits. Nihon Shoki Keitai 2 (508) † | A/B. The prompt's 聳羅 should be **耽羅**. The Japanese reading is Tomura. The Hwangnyongsa list writes it 托羅. |
| Juho | 州胡 주호 | "island barbarians" | most likely Jeju (some say the southwest islands) | Sanguozhi, Han section (3rd c.): a large island in the western sea off Mahan † | A for the 3rd c. Pre-Tamna. Archaic by the 7th c. |
| Gaya polities | 加耶/加羅/伽耶 가야 | the southern confederacy | Nakdong basin | Gwanggaeto Stele: 任那加羅 and 安羅人戍兵 (400) †. Samguk Sagi, Jinheung 23 (562): "加耶叛". Samguk Yusa's 五伽耶 (阿羅, 古寧, 大, 星山, 小). Nihon Shoki Kinmei 23 (562) lists ten: 加羅, 安羅, 斯二岐, 多羅, 卒麻, 古嗟, 子他, 散半下, 乞飡, 稔禮 † | A (stele, Nihon Shoki). The Samguk Yusa "Five Gaya" scheme is a Goryeo systematization (C). |
| Ureuk's twelve tunes | 下加羅都, 上加羅都, 達已, 思勿, 勿慧, 居烈, 沙八兮, 爾赦 … | Gaya place names as song titles | Gaya towns (Geochang = 居烈, Sacheon = 思勿, etc.) | Samguk Sagi, music treatise (Akji) † | B. A lovely period-flavoured way to name Gaya towns. |
| Baekje's "side states" | 叛波, 卓, 多羅, 前羅, 斯羅, 止迷, 麻連, 上己文, 下枕羅 | "small states beside Baekje" | 叛波 = Great Gaya (Goryeong); 卓 = Takseun; 多羅 = Hapcheon; 前羅 = Ara (Haman); 斯羅 = Silla; 止迷, 麻連, 上己文, 下枕羅 = Yeongsan–Seomjin region (下枕羅 maybe Jeju or Gangjin) | Liang tribute scroll 梁職貢圖, Baekje envoy entry (c. 526–539) | A. Baekje's 6th-century boast that Silla is one of its satellites. Great for a Baekje-voiced map. |
| Nakrang / Daebang | 樂浪 낙랑 / 帶方 대방 | Han commanderies | Pyongyang basin / Hwanghae | Samguk Sagi, Goguryeo Micheon 14–15 (313–314) † (taken); Gwanggaeto Stele: 帶方界 (404) † | A as history. By the 6th–7th c. they are **ghost names in Chinese titles**: Northern Qi made Silla's king 樂浪郡公 (Jinheung 26, 565), Tang made Baekje's king 帶方郡王 (624), Northern Qi made Goguryeo's king 遼東郡開國公 (550). |
| Yodong / the Liao | 遼東 요동; 遼水/遼河 | "east of the Liao" | Liaodong peninsula and the Liao River | Throughout the Sui–Tang war entries; Old Book of Tang (645 campaign) | A. In 7th-c. Chinese usage 遼東 is almost a synonym for Goguryeo's western march. |
| Bisa / Yellow Sea crossing | 卑沙城; 東萊, 萊州; 成山/城山; 德物島 | the sea road | Dalian; Laizhou; Chengshan cape; Deokjeok-do | Samguk Sagi, Uija 20 (660): Su Dingfang "crossed the sea from 城山 to 德物島 west of the kingdom" †. Old Book of Tang: Laizhou stores grain on 烏胡島 for the next invasion (648) | A/B. Dengzhou 登州 as a prefecture is late-7th c. (re-established c. 691–692 †). For 640s–660s scenes, 萊州 / 東萊 is safer. |
| Danghang | 党項城 당항성 | Silla's gate to the Tang | Hwaseong, Gyeonggi | Old Book of Tang, Baekje (642): Uija "plans to take 党項城 to cut Silla's road to court" | A. Already in places.ts. |
| Tang overlay (after 660/668) | 熊津都督府; 馬韓, 東明, 金漣, 德安 都督府; 鷄林州都督府; 安東都護府 | Tang's paper map of the peninsula | Baekje (five commands), Silla as "Gyerim prefecture", Goguryeo protectorate at Pyongyang | Samguk Sagi, Uija 20 (five commands); Old Book of Tang (安東都護府, 668). 鷄林州 for Silla (663) † | A. A strong optional layer: the names the empire *tried* to stamp on the three kingdoms. |

## 2. China

| Name | Hanja / Korean | Gloss | Who used it, where | Conf. / caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Heavenly Court | 天朝 천조 | the Tang court | **Chunchu**, Samguk Sagi Jindeok 2 (648): "my country … has served the Heavenly Court for many years" 伏事天朝 | B (speech in a dated annal; may be polished). **The best attested Korean epithet for the Tang court.** |
| The Middle Court | 中朝 중조 | China's court, as a dress standard | Samguk Sagi Jindeok 3 (649): "first wore the robes and caps of the Middle Court" 始服中朝衣冠; Munmu 4 (664), women's dress | B. Neutral and court-flavoured. |
| Hwa / Junghwa | 中華 중화; 華 화 | "the flowered centre" | Samguk Sagi Jindeok 2 (648): Chunchu asks to change Silla's robes "to follow the 中華 system" 以從中華制. Old Book of Tang on Baekje: memorials "follow the 中華 method" | B/A. 華 alone as a country name is rare; 中華 is the attested form. |
| The great country | 大國 대국; 上國 | the Tang (deferential) | Goguryeo refugee envoy to Silla, Munmu 10 (670): "we look only to the 大國" | B. |
| Tang / Great Tang | 唐 당, 大唐 | the dynasty | Queen Jindeok's embroidered ode (650): 大唐開洪業 †; ubiquitous | A/B. |
| Han land | 漢地 한지, 漢國, 漢僧 | China, Chinese monks | **Hyecho** (727): Persians sail "straight to Guangzhou in the Han land" 汎舶漢地 直至廣州; "Han monks" at Kucha and Khotan | A. A Korean eyewitness calling Tang China "Han". Useful for a Buddhist or travel register. |
| China (the term) | 中國 중국 | "the central states" | Kim Busik's commentary (1145) uses it freely. The Liang scroll and Chinese texts use it of China | A in Chinese texts. In Korean mouths of the 7th c. it is plausible but I did not find a securely dated example. Prefer 中朝 or 天朝 in dialogue. |
| Chang'an | 長安 장안; 京師 경사 | the capital | Yijing: a Silla monk "left Chang'an" 出長安. The Samguk Sagi and Tang texts say 京師 ("the capital") | A. Already in places.ts. |
| Luoyang | 洛陽 낙양; 東都 동도 | the eastern capital | Tang texts † | A (Chinese). No special Korean form found. |
| The Southern Dynasties | 宋, 齊, 梁, 陳 (by dynasty name); 吳 오 | the southern courts | Baekje and Silla annals name them by dynasty: Silla Beopheung 8 (521) sends to 梁; Jinheung 26 (565), 陳 sends 1,700 scrolls. **Nihon Shoki Suiko 17 (609): the Baekje king sent monks "to 吳國"** (southern China), blown back by a storm | A/B. 吳 (Japanese *Kure*) is the Japanese–Baekje word for the south. No Korean "Southern Court" 南朝 phrase was found. |
| Yangzhou | 揚州 양주 | Huainan port | Choe Chiwon served under the Huainan governor (9th c.) | C for the 7th c. Leave it off a 7th-c. map, or keep it tiny. |
| Wuyue | 吳越 오월 | 10th-c. coastal kingdom | **Only** in the Hwangnyongsa "nine enemies" list (Samguk Yusa) | **C, anachronistic.** Wuyue existed 907–978. Its presence is one reason scholars date that list to early Goryeo (see §7). |

## 3. Japan

| Name | Hanja / Korean | Gloss | Earliest attestation | Conf. / caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wa | 倭 왜 | the islands' realm | Gwanggaeto Stele (repeatedly, 391–404) †; Chilji-do inscription: "made for the Wa king" 爲倭王旨造 †; Silla Silseong 1 (402) hostage to Wa † | A. Default for any scene before 670. |
| Ilbon | 日本 일본 | "origin of the sun" | **Samguk Sagi Munmu 10 (670), 12th month: 倭國更號日本 自言近日所出以爲名** ("Wa changed its name to Ilbon; they say it is because they are near where the sun comes out"). Copied from the New Book of Tang. The Baekje émigré Ye Gun's epitaph (678, Xi'an) already has 日本 † | A/B. Use from 670. The Samguk Yusa uses 日本 anachronistically for older events (e.g., Yeono-rang). |
| Where the sun rises / sets | 日出處 / 日沒處 | Wa's self-styling vs. Sui | Book of Sui, Wa (607 letter): "the Son of Heaven where the sun rises, to the Son of Heaven where the sun sets" | A. Japanese-authored, not Korean, but it is the real ancestor of the "Eastern/Western court" idea (see §8). |
| Eastern Heavenly Sovereign / Western Emperor | 東天皇 / 西皇帝 | | Nihon Shoki Suiko 16 (608), 9th month: 東天皇敬白西皇帝 | A as text (720). Some scholars think the wording is the compilers' retouch. |
| Bodhisattva Son of Heaven west of the sea | 海西菩薩天子 | Wa's name for the Sui emperor | Book of Sui, Wa (607) | A. Lovely, Buddhist; China as "west of the sea". |
| Yamato | 大和 / 倭 (やまと) | the Nara-basin court | Nihon Shoki (writes 倭 or 日本, read *Yamato*) | A in Japan. No Korean source of the era writes "Yamato"; Koreans wrote 倭. |
| Tsukushi | 筑紫 축자 | northern Kyushu | Nihon Shoki: the Sui envoy "reached Tsukushi"; "the Tsukushi governor" 筑紫大宰 (609) | A (Nihon Shoki). Not found in the Samguk Sagi. Already in places.ts. |
| Naniwa | 難波 난파 | Osaka bay port | Nihon Shoki Suiko 16 (608): a new guesthouse built "above the **Goguryeo guesthouse** at Naniwa" 難波高麗館; Sui envoys moor at 難波津. **Baekje wooden tablet, Ssangbuk-ri, Buyeo: 那尒波連公**, read as a man of the Naniwa clan serving in Sabi | A. The Naniwa mokgan is a real Baekje-side trace of a Japanese name. |
| Tsushima | 對馬 대마 | the strait island | Samguk Sagi Silseong 7 (408): "the Wa set up camp on 對馬島" † | B. Already in places.ts. |
| Fusang | 扶桑 부상 | the mulberry land of sunrise | Book of Liang: 扶桑國, 20,000 li east (monk Huishen, 499) †; Ye Gun epitaph (678) uses 扶桑 for the Wa refuge of Baekje loyalists † | A as a Chinese mythic geography. Excellent Eastern Ocean label (§7). |
| The Hairy People | 毛人 모인 | eastern barbarians of the islands (Emishi) | Book of Song, Wa king Bu's letter (478): "east, I conquered 55 lands of hairy men" †. Same letter calls Korea **海北** "north of the sea" | A. A Wa world map in one sentence. |

**How Japan named Korea (Nihon Shoki).** 百濟 Kudara, 新羅 Shiragi, 高麗 Koma (Goguryeo), 任那 Mimana, 加羅 Kara, 耽羅 Tomura; 熊津 also as 久麻那利 Kumanari (Yūryaku 21) †; 白村江 Hakusukinoe (the White River, 663) †; 州柔 Tsunu (= 周留城) †. Korea as a whole: 西蕃 "the western vassals" and 海北 / 海表. The 548 entry adds a gloss that "all the 西蕃 call the Japanese ruler 可畏天皇": a Japanese claim, not a Korean usage.

## 4. The steppe and the west

| Name | Hanja / Korean | Gloss | Modern identification | Earliest attestation | Conf. / caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Turks | 突厥 돌궐 | Türk khaganates | Mongolia to the Aral | **Samguk Sagi Goguryeo Yangwon 7 (551), 9th month: 突厥來圍新城不克 移攻白巖城** (General Go Heul beats them). Yeongyang 18 (607): a Goguryeo envoy found in the Qimin Khagan's tent when Sui Yangdi arrives †. Hyecho: Turkish kings ruling Gandhara, Kapisa, Zabul | B for 551 (date disputed: the Turks only broke the Rouran in 552; some move it to 555+ or call it fiction). A in Hyecho. |
| Tiele / Uighur | 鐵勒 철륵 / 回紇 회흘 | Turkic confederation; its lead tribe | Mongolia | Chinese only. One historian argues the Afrasiab envoys went via the Tiele revolt of 660–663 | No Korean attestation of 回紇 in the era found. Use 鐵勒 if anything. |
| Xueyantuo | 薛延陀 설연타 | steppe khaganate, 630s–646 | Mongolia | Zizhi Tongjian / Tang texts: in 645 Yeon Gaesomun tried to buy Xueyantuo help against Tang † | A (Chinese). A good Gesomun hook; not in Korean sources that I found. |
| Tuyuhun | 吐谷渾 토욕혼 | Xianbei kingdom at Koko Nor | Qinghai | Chinese only. Collapsed under Tibet in the 660s | No Korean-source attestation found. Optional. |
| Tubo (Tibet) | 吐蕃 토번 (Hyecho also 土蕃) | the Tibetan empire | Tibetan plateau | **Yijing: the Silla monk 玄太 "took the Tibet road" 取吐蕃道 in the Yonghui era (650–655).** Hyecho: Great Bolor, Yangtong and Sapoci are "under Tibet"; Tibetans live in felt tents among ice mountains and "do not know the Buddha's law" | A. **Not named in the Samguk Sagi** (its Munmu chapters carry Xue Rengui's letter but no Tibet entry). Tibet's 670 defeat of Xue Rengui at Dafei River and the 676 invasion pulled Tang armies off the peninsula; Korean historians lean on that heavily. |
| The Western Regions | 西域 서역 | the lands west of the Jade Gate | Tarim basin and beyond | Yijing's title; Korean monks "travelled the 西域" | A. |
| The Flowing Sands | 流沙 유사 | the desert road | Gobi / Taklamakan | **Choe Chiwon's lion-dance poem, in the Samguk Sagi music treatise: "He crossed the Flowing Sands, ten thousand li, to come here" 遠涉流沙萬里來** | B (9th-c. poem preserved in the Samguk Sagi). **A superb, Korean-voiced desert label.** |
| Khotan | 于闐 우전; 月顚 월전? | jade city | Hotan, Xinjiang | Hyecho: "a Han temple at Khotan". Choe Chiwon's dance 月顚 is usually read as Khotan. Haedong Goseungjeon: the Silla monk Anham returned in 605 with Khotanese monks † | A (Hyecho). 月顚 = Khotan is a scholarly reading. Haedong Goseungjeon is 1215. |
| Kucha / Anxi | 龜茲 구자; 安西 안서 | seat of the Protectorate of the Pacified West | Kuqa, Xinjiang | Hyecho arrived at 安西 in the 11th month of 727; lists the "Four Garrisons" 安西, 于闐, 疎勒, 焉耆 | A. |
| Kashgar, Karashahr | 疏勒/疎勒 소륵; 焉耆/烏耆 언기 | Tarim oases | Kashi; Yanqi | Hyecho | A. |
| The Pamirs | 葱嶺 총령 | "the Onion Range" | Pamir knot | Hyecho: 葱嶺鎮, "the Han call it 葱嶺" | A. A natural border marker for the map. |
| Sogdiana / Samarkand | 康國 강국 (+ 安國, 曹國, 史國, 石騾國, 米國) | "the Hu countries" | Samarkand, Bukhara, Kesh, Tashkent, Maymurgh | **Hyecho: east of the Arabs "are all Hu countries: 安國, 曹國, 史國, 石騾國, 米國, 康國"**; "only 康國 has a temple". **Afrasiab mural**: two envoys with bird-feather caps (조우관) and ring-pommel swords at King Varkhuman's court | A. Majority view: Goguryeo envoys, c. 650s–660s. Tang made Varkhuman governor of 康居都督府 in 658. Debate: did they really go, or is it a Sogdian world-picture? Silla or Balhae are minority readings. |
| Sogdians (dance) | 束毒 속독 | "Sogdian" masked dance | | Choe Chiwon, Samguk Sagi music treatise | B. Scholarly reading 束毒 = Soghd. |
| Ferghana, Khuttal, Wakhan, Shighnan | 跋賀那, 骨咄, 胡蜜, 識匿 | | Central Asian valleys | Hyecho | A. Detail only. |
| Tokharistan | 吐火羅 토화라 | | Bactria (Balkh) | Hyecho: its king fled; Arab troops occupy it | A. |
| Persia | 波斯 파사 | Sasanian Iran | Iran | **Liang tribute scroll (c. 526–539) paints a 波斯國 envoy in the same scroll as the Baekje envoy.** **Hyecho: 波斯國 "once ruled the Arabs, who were its camel-herders; they rebelled, killed the king, and now Persia is swallowed by the Arabs"**; Persians sail to Ceylon, Kunlun and Guangzhou | A. Persia fell 651. For a 7th-c. map, Persia is *falling*. |
| The Arabs | 大食 대식 (Hyecho writes 大寔) | the caliphate | Arabia, Iraq, Iran | Hyecho, throughout (Arab armies in Sindh, Tokharistan, Persia) | A. Hyecho's form is 大寔. |
| Fulin (Byzantium) | 拂菻 불림 (Hyecho: **大拂臨** "Great Fulin", 小拂臨 "Little Fulin") | Rome | Constantinople / Byzantine empire | **Hyecho: "northwest along the sea from Little Fulin is Great Fulin; its armies are strong; the Arabs attacked it many times and failed; the Turks failed too"** | A (hearsay; he did not go). The prompt's 拂菰 should be **拂菻**. "Little Fulin" is usually read as Byzantine Syria / the Levant under the Arabs. |
| Daqin | 大秦 대진 | Rome (Han-era name) | | Han–Jin Chinese histories | **No Korean attestation of the era found.** By the 7th c. Tang and Hyecho say 拂菻. Prefer 불림. |
| Dunhuang | 敦煌 돈황 | | Gansu | Hyecho's manuscript **survived there** (found by Pelliot, 1908) | No Korean mention of Dunhuang found; the manuscript itself is the link. |

## 7. Cosmological and mythic places

| Name | Hanja / Korean | What it is | Attestation | Conf. / caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Heaven | 天 천; 天帝 | the sky lord of the founding myths | **Gwanggaeto Stele: Chumo is "son of the Heavenly Emperor" 天帝之子 and of the River Lord's daughter; a yellow dragon 黃龍 carries him up.** Moduru epitaph: "grandson of the River Lord, son of sun and moon" 河泊之孫 日月之子. Samguk Yusa: 桓因 (glossed as Indra), 桓雄 at 太伯山 神檀樹, 神市 † | A for Goguryeo (5th c.). The Dangun myth is first written c. 1280 (M). |
| Trayastrimsa | 忉利天 도리천 | the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, atop Sumeru | Samguk Yusa: Queen Seondeok asks to be buried "in 忉利天", south of Nangsan; Sacheonwangsa (Four Heavenly Kings) is later built below it, putting her tomb above the Four Kings † | B/M. **The best attested Buddhist-heaven place tied to a 7th-c. queen.** |
| Mount Sumeru | 須彌山 수미산 | the world mountain | Implied by the 忉利天 / Sacheonwangsa layout. A Silla envoy of 670 is literally named 須彌山 (Kim Sumisan) in Munmu 10 | B. Not named as a place in the annals that I found. |
| Western Paradise | 西方 서방, 極樂 극락 | Amitabha's Pure Land | Samguk Yusa hyangga 願往生歌 (attributed to Munmu's reign): "Moon, are you going to the West now?" 西方念丁 去賜里遣 † | B/M. The cleanest 7th-c.-attributed Korean "West". |
| The Three Divine Mountains | 三神山: 蓬萊, 方丈, 瀛洲 | Daoist isles of immortals in the Eastern Sea | **Samguk Sagi Baekje Mu 35 (634): the palace pond's island "modelled on Mount Fangzhang of the immortals" 擬方丈仙山.** The Baekje gilt-bronze incense burner shows a Boshan-style immortals' mountain † | B. Strong. Penglai alone is not named in Korean annals that I found; use **方丈** for a Baekje-voiced label. |
| Silla's Three Mountains | 三山: 奈歷 (奈林), 骨火, 穴禮 | the great sacrifices | Samguk Sagi sacrifice treatise (祭祀志): 大祀 | B. These are the chronicle's Narim, Golhwa and Hyullé. The list is post-unification, but the cult is older. |
| Silla's Five Peaks | 五岳: 吐含山 (E), 地理山 (S), 雞龍山 (W), 太伯山 (N), 父岳/公山 (centre) | 中祀 | Samguk Sagi sacrifice treatise | B, **late 7th c. or later** (it includes old Baekje's Gyeryong). Don't use it for pre-660 scenes. |
| Silla's Four Seas | 四海: 阿等邊 (E), 兄邊 (S), 未陵邊 (W), 非禮山 (N) | Silla's own "four seas" shrines | Same treatise | B. A ready-made Korean "Four Seas" ring for the map. |
| Dragon palace of the Eastern Sea | 龍宮 용궁; 東海 | sea-dragon realm | Samguk Sagi Munmu 21 (681): buried "on the great rock at the Eastern Sea's mouth; folk say he became a dragon" †. Samguk Yusa: the Manpasikjeok flute from a floating isle in the Eastern Sea (682) †. Hwangnyongsa stands "south of the 龍宮" in Gyeongju | B/M. |
| Talhae's homeland | 多婆那國 다파나국 (Samguk Yusa: 龍城國) | sea kingdom | Samguk Sagi Talhae 1: "a thousand li northeast of Wa" † | B/M. An Eastern Ocean myth-land. |
| Land of Giants | 長人國 장인 | giants beyond Silla's eastern pass | **New Book of Tang, Silla: "to the east it holds off the Giants (東拒長人) … three zhang tall, saw teeth, hooked claws, black hair … Silla always keeps several thousand crossbowmen at the iron-gated pass"** | A (Tang-era report). Recent work reads it as Silla's image of Balhae. **Perfect Eastern-frontier myth label.** |
| Fusang | 扶桑 부상 | the sunrise mulberry land | Book of Liang † | A (Chinese myth geography). |
| Western Flower Field | 서천꽃밭 (西天 + 꽃밭) | garden of rebirth flowers and killing flowers at the world's western edge | Jeju 이공본풀이, 세경본풀이, 문전본풀이; Bari myths. **Recorded only in the 20th century** (Akiba–Akamatsu 1930s; Hyeon Yong-jun 1980; Jin Seong-gi 1991). A related Buddhist tale, 안락국태자경, is printed in the Worin Seokbo (1459) **without** a flower field. One scholar links the plot to a Jirimsa founding legend he dates to 643 | **M, not attested in the Three Kingdoms era.** 西天 is the Buddhist name for India, so the place name is at least Buddhist-era. The project's hanja 西天花田 is a modern coinage; the songs say 서천꽃밭. Fine for a myth layer; don't present it as a 7th-c. term. |
| Underworld | 저승 (native); 冥府, 冥界, 黃泉 | land of the dead | 저승 is attested only in the Hangul era (15th c. onward) †. Hyecho's elegy speaks of the "dark road" 冥路 | M/C. For an era-flavoured label, 冥府 or 冥路 is safer in hanja; 저승 is fine as the Korean folk word. |

**The Hwangnyongsa "nine enemies" (九韓).** The Samguk Yusa quotes Anhong's 東都成立記: each storey of the pagoda (built 645) subdues one neighbour: 1 日本, 2 中華, 3 吳越, 4 托羅 (Tamna), 5 鷹遊 (unclear; read as Baekje, an island state, or the Ryukyus/Taiwan), 6 靺鞨, 7 丹國 (Khitan), 8 女狄 (Jurchen), 9 穢貊. It is the most famous "Silla world map" in one sentence. **But** 日本, 吳越 (907–978) and 女狄 do not fit 645. A 2023 KCI study dates the list to 936–978 (early Goryeo). Use it as Goryeo hindsight, not as Seondeok's list.

## 8. Directional and world-view terms

| Term | Hanja / Korean | Meaning | Attestation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Haedong | 海東 해동 | "East of the Sea" | **Tang Gaozong's letter to Uija (651): "the three kingdoms east of the sea (海東三國) were founded long ago … their borders interlock like dog's teeth"**; same letter: "the people of the Three Han" 三韓之氓, "the three vassals" 三蕃. Uija was called "the Zengzi (or Zeng and Min) of Haedong" 海東曾子 / 海東曾閔 † | A. A Tang-coined frame the Koreans adopted. **Great cosmology label for the peninsula as a whole.** |
| Samhan | 三韓 삼한 | the Three Han → the three kingdoms | Tang letter (651) uses 三韓 for all three. Silla's "unified the Three Han" 一統三韓: Samguk Sagi Sinmun 12 (692), the temple-name dispute. Cheongju Uncheon-dong stele: 合三韓而廣地, traditionally c. 686 | A for 三韓 = the three kingdoms (651). The **"unification" claim is contested**: one scholar dates the Uncheon-dong stele to the 9th–10th c. and the 一統三韓 idea to late Silla / Goryeo. |
| Four Seas | 四海 사해 | the known world | **Gwanggaeto Stele: "his martial might shook the Four Seas" 武威振被四海.** Silla's own 四海 shrines (sacrifice treatise) | A. Goguryeo-centred. |
| All under heaven | 天下 천하 | the world, ruled by one | **Moduru epitaph: "all under heaven, the four quarters, know this land is most holy" 天下四方知此國郡最聖.** Goguryeo loyalists to Silla, Munmu 10 (670): "reviving fallen states is the common justice of 天下" 興滅國繼絶世 天下之公義也 | A (epitaph). Goguryeo had its own 天下 centred on itself (the "Goguryeo tianxia" theory). |
| Eastern Yi | 東夷 동이 | "eastern barbarians" | **Jungwon Goguryeo Stele: 東夷寐錦**, Goguryeo's name for Silla's king. Samguk Yusa: Manjushri says Silla's king is "not like the 東夷 共工 lineage". Chinese histories' 東夷傳 | A. Who calls whom 東夷 is the whole politics: Goguryeo calls Silla that; China calls all three that. |
| Eastern/Western vassal | 東蕃 / 西蕃 | | Taizong's letter to Baekje (627) calls it the "eastern vassal" 撫有東蕃. The Nihon Shoki calls the Korean states 西蕃 | A. |
| Middle Court | 中朝 | China | Samguk Sagi Jindeok 3 (649) | B. See §2. |
| Heavenly Court | 天朝 | Tang | Chunchu, Jindeok 2 (648) | B. See §2. |
| Haebuk | 海北 | Korea, from Japan | Wa king Bu's letter (478) †; Nihon Shoki 海北彌移居 | A. |

### Are "Western Court" (서조) and "Eastern Court" (동조) attested?

**No, not as Korean phrasings.** No 6th–7th-century Korean source I could find calls China the 西朝 or Japan the 東朝. The closest real phrasings:

- **Japan's** letters to Sui: "the Son of Heaven where the sun sets" 日沒處天子 (Book of Sui, 607) and "the Western Emperor" 西皇帝 (Nihon Shoki, 608). The Sui court was also "the Bodhisattva Son of Heaven west of the sea" 海西菩薩天子. These are Japanese, and they cast China as the West.
- **Korean** terms for the Tang court are 天朝 (the Heavenly Court), 中朝 (the Middle Court), 大國 (the great country), and Hyecho's 漢地 (Han land).
- For Japan, the Samguk Sagi gives 近日所出 (near where the sun comes out, 670).

Two cautions for a hanja-literate reader:

1. In classical Chinese, **東朝** usually meant the **crown prince's** household (or the empress dowager's), not an eastern country.
2. In 6th-century Chinese writing, **東朝/西朝** could mean the rival Eastern and Western Wei courts. So "the Eastern Court" for Wa is the chronicle's invention.

It is a defensible invention: it echoes Japan's own 東天皇/西皇帝 pairing. It should not be sold as a period term.

## 10. Notes on the project's current labels

- **Hwa 華 / "The Western Court" 서조.** The epithet is invented (see §8). 華 alone is thin as a country name; 中華 is what Chunchu says.
- **Wa 倭 / "The Eastern Court" 동조.** Invented. 東朝 reads as "the crown prince's court" to a hanja eye. 倭 is correct before 670 and 日本 after.
- **Tamna.** The correct hanja is 耽羅. The prompt had 聳羅. In `places.ts` the entry `mugun` carries hanja 耽羅. That's fine if Mugun is meant to be a Tamna place, but worth a glance.
- **Fulin.** Correct hanja 拂菻; Hyecho writes 拂臨. The prompt had 拂菰.
- **Daqin 大秦.** No Korean attestation in the era; Fulin is the period word.
- **Dengzhou 登州.** As a prefecture it is late-7th-century †. For the 640s–660s crossings, 萊州/東萊 and the 成山/城山 cape are safer.
- **Western Flower Field 西天花田.** The hanja is a modern coinage, and the concept is recorded only in the 20th century. As a myth layer it is fine.

---

## 11. Recommendations for the zoomed-out cosmology layer

The principle: prefer a label a 6th–7th-century Korean (or a Korean traveller) actually wrote. Where the chronicle keeps an invented epithet, keep it in the English layer and give the Korean or hanja line the attested form.

**Keep, with the best attested label**

| Region | Recommended label (EN / KO / hanja) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| China | **Hwa — "The Heavenly Court"** / 천조 / 天朝 (alt. "The Middle Court" 중조 中朝) | Chunchu's own word, 648; 中朝 is the neutral annal word, 649. If you keep "The Western Court", mark it in-world as a Wa-style idiom. |
| Japan | **Wa — "Where the Sun Comes Up"** / 해 뜨는 곳 / 近日所出 (or 日出處); switch the name to Ilbon 日本 from 670 | Samguk Sagi 670 gives exactly this, and the Sui letter's 日出處 backs it. |
| India | **The Five Indias** / 오천축 / 五天竺 | Hyecho's title; a Korean word. |
| Persia | **Persia** / 파사 / 波斯 | Hyecho and the Liang scroll. For the 7th c., tag it as "falling to the Arabs" (651). |
| Rome | **Great Fulin** / 대불림 / 大拂臨 (standard 拂菻) | Hyecho's form; drop 大秦. |
| Turks | **The Turks** / 돌궐 / 突厥 | Samguk Sagi 551; Hyecho. |
| Tibet | **Tubo** / 토번 / 吐蕃 | Yijing (650s) and Hyecho. |
| Steppe | **The Northern Plains** is fine as a region label; scatter 突厥, 鐵勒 and (for pre-552 scenes) 蠕蠕 | |
| Pacific | **The Eastern Sea** / 동해 / 東海 for the near water; the **Land of Giants** 長人 and **Fusang** 扶桑 as myth marks farther out | New Book of Tang; Book of Liang. |
| SE Asia | **The Southern Sea** / 남해 / 南海, with **Kunlun** 崑崙 as the people-label | Yijing, Hyecho. |

**Add (highest value first)**

1. **The Arabs** / 대식 / 大食 (Hyecho 大寔). Without them the 7th-c. west makes no sense: they are eating Persia in the chronicle's own decades.
2. **Samarkand** / 강국 / 康國. The one western court that painted Koreans (Afrasiab). A natural pin for a Gesomun-era envoy thread.
3. **The Flowing Sands** / 유사 / 流沙. Korean-voiced (Choe Chiwon's lion "crossed the Flowing Sands, ten thousand li"). The desert band between Tang and the west.
4. **The Pamirs** / 총령 / 葱嶺 and **Anxi** / 안서 / 安西 (Kucha), where Hyecho's road ended. They give the Silk Road a Korean endpoint.
5. **Haedong** / 해동 / 海東 as the cosmological name of the peninsula ("the three kingdoms east of the sea", Tang 651), with **Samhan** 三韓 beneath it.
6. **Srivijaya** / 실리불서 / 室利佛逝 and **Lion Country** / 사자국 / 師子國. Real Korean deaths and Korean-described ports in the Southern Sea.
7. **The Land of Giants** / 장인국 / 長人. A Tang-recorded Silla legend: a mythic eastern frontier with an iron gate and crossbowmen. Pure chronicle fuel.
8. **Mount Fangzhang** / 방장선산 / 方丈仙山 (Baekje 634) in the Eastern Ocean, as the Daoist immortals' isle. It is attested in a Korean palace garden.
9. **Trayastrimsa Heaven** / 도리천 / 忉利天 above the map (Seondeok's chosen heaven). It pairs with the Western Paradise 西方.
10. **The Ghost Commanderies**, optional for a politics layer: 樂浪 (Silla's Chinese title), 帶方 (Baekje's), 遼東 (Goguryeo's), and after 660/668 the Tang paper overlay 熊津都督府 / 鷄林州 / 安東都護府.

**Use with care or leave off**

- **Hwangnyongsa "nine enemies"**: early Goryeo hindsight; don't voice it in Seondeok's court as written.
- **Wuyue, Yangzhou, Uighur, Tuyuhun, Linyi, Zhenla, Daqin**: either too late or with no Korean attestation of the era.
- **Five Peaks 五岳**: post-660 only. **一統三韓**: a contested late-7th-to-9th-century slogan.
- **Western Flower Field / 저승**: keep them in the myth layer, styled as myth, not as period geography.

## 12. The nine human nations (wiki, Nov 2026)

The chronicle treats these as civilizations, not as one dynasty’s borders. Two rings, counted from the peninsula. Softness grows with distance.

- **Near Lands · 옆나라:** Samhan, Japan (`wa`), China (`hwa`), Northern Nomads. Each has a sharp heartland and a slightly wider reach.
- **Far Lands · 먼나라:** Tibet, India, Persia/Daesik, Rome, Southern Seas. Each has a definite heartland (the plateau; the Indic core; the plateau then the caliphate’s core; the Byzantine heartland; the sea road) and a fuzzier civilizational reach (subject valleys; broader South Asia; the wider Middle East; more of Europe and northern Africa; the harbours past Srivijaya).

Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla and Gaya stay polity pages inside Samhan. Turks stay inside the northern world (map label `turks` is a people line, not a nation). Persia and Daesik are one article with a rename at 651.

| World | Wiki id | Korean / hanja | Record to lead with |
|---|---|---|---|
| Samhan / Joseon | `samhan` | 삼한 三韓; also 해동 海東, and 조선 朝鮮 as the older name | Tang letter, 651 (海東三國, 三韓之氓). Samguk Sagi, Jindeok 3 (649), 中朝衣冠. Sanguozhi Dongyi for Buyeo white and the Goguryeo jeolpung. Yijing 691 on feathered caps. |
| Japan | `wa` (Ilbon from 670) | 왜 倭 → 일본 日本 | Gwanggaeto Stele. Book of Sui, 607 letter. Samguk Sagi, Munmu 10 (670): 倭國更號日本. Wei account of the unsewn cross-cloth; Book of Sui on the white head-cloth. Nihon Shoki is secondary. |
| China | `hwa` | 천조 天朝; also 화 華, 중조 中朝, 중화 中華, 한지 漢地 | Samguk Sagi, Jindeok 2 (648): 天朝, 中華制. Jindeok 3: 中朝衣冠. Hyecho: 漢地. |
| Northern Nomads | `northern-nomads` | 북적 北狄. Map label was 막북 漠北, “Northern Plains.” | Book of Sui, Mohe (seven tribes) and Turks. Samguk Sagi, Yangwon 7 (551), 突厥. Hyecho on Turkish kings in Gandhara. Kül Tegin, 732, Bökli. Jurchen is a later name for the forest half. |
| Tibet | `tubo` | 토번 吐蕃 (Hyecho also 土蕃) | Yijing: 取吐蕃道, Yonghui years. Hyecho: felt tents, ice, lands under Tibet. |
| India | `cheonchuk` | 천축 天竺; 오천축 五天竺. Parallel with 천조. | Hyecho, 往五天竺國傳 (727). Yijing: Aryavarman at Nalanda. |
| Persia / Daesik | `persia` (stage `daesik` from 651) | 파사 波斯 → 대식 大食 (Hyecho 大寔) | Liang tribute scroll, Persian envoy beside Baekje. Hyecho: Persia swallowed; Persians still sail. |
| Rome | `bullim` | 불림 拂菻; 대불림 大拂臨. Not 불름. 대진 大秦 is the Han-era name. | Hyecho on Great Fulin and Little Fulin. No Korean annal uses 大秦. |
| Southern Seas | `southern-seas` | 남해 南海; people-word 곤륜 崑崙 | Yijing: two Silla monks die at 室利佛逝. Hyecho: 南海, 崑崙國. Nihon Shoki, Kinmei 4, Funan goods (secondary). |

Map `nation` ids match the wiki: `samhan`, `wa`, `hwa`, `northern-nomads`, `tubo`, `cheonchuk`, `persia` (label `daesik` from 651), `bullim`, `southern-seas`. Region washes still use `nomads`, `tibet`, `india`, `rome`, `sea`. `turks`, `khitan` and `jurchen` are people lines hosted on `northern-nomads`.
